title: Home-Grown Management
coreMove: Build internal leadership capacity so authority carries institutional memory and values, while still testing competence instead of rewarding tenure.
sourcePressure: The sidecar supports internal leadership development, continuity, institutional design, and avoiding dependence on imported saviors.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating home-grown management as promotion-from-within sentimentality or anti-outsider bias, rather than a deliberate pipeline for values plus judgment.

sourceAnchors.name: Home-grown management
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar supports internal leadership development as a chapter-level concept and warns against dependence on imported saviors
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The next leader should not arrive as a rescue mission; the institution should have been teaching its future for years.

counterintuition: succession starts long before the vacancy
examples: loading dock clock and outside rescuer

exampleSpecs.domain: regional dialysis network preparing clinic managers before a retirement wave
exampleSpecs.audience: Ryan, operations director with six senior nurses nearing retirement
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients need consistent care standards across clinics after experienced managers leave
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ryan maps which charge nurses have run budget, staffing, and values-pressure drills, then starts rotations before the retirements become emergencies
exampleSpecs.firstImage: six retirement dates marked on a clinic coverage map

exampleSpecs.domain: family-owned logistics firm choosing a depot manager after an outside candidate impresses investors
exampleSpecs.audience: Pavel, COO balancing investor pressure and route knowledge
exampleSpecs.stakes: a depot can hit metrics while destroying the dispatch trust that keeps drivers honest
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Who has handled a storm closure at 3 a.m.?" Pavel asks, then evaluates internal candidates on tested judgment rather than tenure alone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: route maps and storm-closure logs on a depot table

exampleSpecs.domain: independent school building department chairs through observed parent-conference practice
exampleSpecs.audience: Margaux, head of school after two failed external hires
exampleSpecs.stakes: academic standards and parent trust suffer when chairs learn the culture after appointment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Margaux watches teacher candidates handle a simulated angry parent conference before naming a chair, making cultural judgment visible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: empty parent chairs arranged under student art

exampleSpecs.domain: cybersecurity firm creating incident commanders from inside rotating response cells
exampleSpecs.audience: Akira, practice lead whose founder still gets every crisis call
exampleSpecs.stakes: clients wait during incidents because command authority has not been grown
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Akira predicts who can command without the founder, then runs a live-fire drill that gives authority to the internal cell lead
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Who gives the order when the founder's phone is off?
mustAvoid: technical brilliance substituted for command readiness

exampleSpecs.domain: regional food bank developing warehouse leads through donor, safety, and volunteer rotations
exampleSpecs.audience: Hannah, executive director facing growth in demand
exampleSpecs.stakes: a new warehouse head must protect dignity with donors, volunteers, and clients at once
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Hannah one chaotic distribution day to see that the best forklift operator had never been tested with donor pressure, so she builds rotations before promotion
exampleSpecs.firstImage: pallet tags curling on a warehouse door after a long distribution shift

exampleSpecs.domain: city parks department grooming district supervisors through winter, festival, and budget assignments
exampleSpecs.audience: Olivier, deputy commissioner replacing three retiring supervisors
exampleSpecs.stakes: parks can look fine in summer while leadership gaps appear in storms and budget cuts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Olivier move promising crew leads through winter storm duty and festival cleanup before promotion, so continuity includes tested range
exampleSpecs.firstImage: snowplow keys, festival permits, and a budget binder on one desk

skillTargets: distinguish memory plus values from mere tenure
spot when external rescue hides weak institution-building

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one role that would hurt if vacant tomorrow. Write the three experiences someone inside must complete before they can inherit it.
sourceAnchorsNote: Frozen source sidecars for this book expose concept support and source artifacts, but little chapter-level anecdote detail after chapter 1. Use only the anchors listed here; do not invent company histories, named executives, studies, or dates.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
